Connor  thanks for the packet. High-level legal assessment:

- Warranty: Their requested deletion of our limited warranty replaces it with an open promise to "ensure results." We should not accept language that creates open-ended performance warranties. Keep a limited warranty tied to the SOW deliverables with remedies limited to re-performance and service credits.

- Indemnity: The proposed broad indemnity (covering third-party IP claims even when Medicore alters the product) would significantly enlarge our exposure. Two mitigation paths appear reasonable for exec consideration:
  1) Money cap at $1.5M aggregate for all liability (excluding claims for gross negligence/willful misconduct) + preserve our IP misuse carveouts; and require Medicore to maintain CGL & cyber insurance with minimum limits (we should specify carriers/limits).
  2) If execs will not accept a full cap, require a narrower indemnity limited to claims arising from Redwood's software and services as delivered (not customer's modifications).

I will mark the SOW redline with the exact language options and prepare a one-page memo summarizing worst-case exposures and residual risk. From Legals perspective, option 1 with clear insurance requirements is acceptable to escalate for exec approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
